Where do I go to enroll online?

Students that are interested in enrolling should select the course from the course catalog (opens in new tab). Once you have selected your course, please click "enroll now" which will take you to the intake form to complete the enrollment process. Prior to enrolling, please coordinate with your local school counselor concerning the local school policies and other requirements.

Purchase & Pay

When it is time to purchase additional courses, parents can click Purchase & Pay to gain access to the internal catalog. The catalog gives the parent the ability to search via the subject for the course/CBE. To ensure that students are being enrolled in the correct course, Texas Tech K-12 asks that Parents of Full-time students check with their Texas Tech K-12 advisor prior to completing any enrollments. Parents of Supplemental students should check with their students school Counselor to ensure enrollment into the correct course/CBE. Once a student submits an assignment for grading, they are no longer eligible for a refund in the tuition-paid or supplemental programs.

Once you find the course you want, click "Add to Cart". It will show "Added to Cart" and appear on the right-hand side.

When you've added all courses, click "Complete Checkout" to go to the checkout process and finish payment.

After pressing "Complete Checkout", you should receive notification that you are being directed to Touchnet to complete payment information.

Upon entering payment information, the following screen should display:

If payment is successful, you should receive a copy of the receipt:

Selecting the Customer Ledger will all you to view the student's payment information. You may also export the ledger to excel or print out a copy.

Where do I go to enroll online?

Students that are interested in enrolling should select the course from the course catalog (opens in new tab). Prior to enrolling, please coordinate with your local school counselor concerning the local school policies and other requirements.

How do I get started with a Course or Credit By Exam (CBE)?

How do I get started with a Course or Credit By Exam (CBE)?

Upon completion of the course, student's will be ale to view the overall course grade in the portal. You may also print out a copy of the grade report.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) Use Policy

This policy covers any generative AI tool, such as ChatGTP, Elicit, Photo Math, etc. This includes text and artwork/graphics/video/audio, etc.

All work submitted in this course must be your own. You may not use artificial intelligence tools to complete your assignments in this course.

If an instructor suspects that an assignment is not the work of the student, it will receive a score of zero. The instructor will message the student or provide feedback on the assignment indicating the need to schedule a one-on-one video conference, during which the student will be required to demonstrate their skills or knowledge through an alternative or mutually agreed-upon assignment. The grade of the alternate or agreed upon assignment will be determined at the instructor’s discretion with the highest possible score being 70%.

If it is determined that a student has violated final exam directions on Final Exam Set 1 or CBE Set 1, the exam will be scored as zero. The student may take Final Exam Set 2 or CBE Set 2 with the highest possible score being 70%.

The incident will be reported to Texas Tech K-12 Administration and documented in the student’s file. Continued violations of Texas Tech University’s Academic Integrity Policy will result in the removal of the student from the program. Texas Tech Student Handbook (opens in new tab).

Taking a Course

Texas Tech K-12 does not operate on a semester basis; therefore, courses are asynchronous. Open enrollment allows you to enroll in any course, at any time, and work at your own pace. If you are enrolled in another district, obtain approval from your school counselor before enrolling in a course to ensure credit upon successful completion.

The majority of courses are offered online through our Course Portal (opens in new tab). For a full listing of courses and course descriptions offered by Texas Tech K-12, visit the Texas Tech K-12 Course Catalog (opens in new tab).

Purchase & Pay

The Purchase & Pay tab will allow you to purchase and pay for your enrollments with Texas Tech K-12. The catalog gives the parent the ability to search via the subject for the course/CBE (Please note that students apart of the Texas Tech K-12 Tuition Free program will not have access to Purchase & Pay). Once you have found the course that you are enrolling in, please select "Add to Cart". The course will show "Added to Cart" while the course will appear on the right hand side.

Once all courses have been selected, please press "Checkout" which will take you to the Checkout process to complete course payment.

After pressing "Checkout", you should receive notification that you are being directed to Touchnet to complete payment information.

Upon entering payment information, you should receive payment confirmation.

Clicking on continue, you should receive your receipt as well as the option to print it out.

Access the Canvas dashboard

**Accessing the Texas Tech K-12 Course Catalog**

- Students can view available courses and Credit By Exams (CBEs) in the Texas Tech K-12 Course Catalog online.
- To access the catalog, visit the Texas Tech K-12 Course Catalog [here](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/courses/catalog/).

**Next Step**
- Before enrolling, students should confirm with their local school counselor that credit will be awarded for the selected course or CBE.

If you need further assistance, you can contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.

Q: How does only ranking the Top 10% benefit students in the top quarter of students who are very close to the Top 10%?

When a student does not have a rank, a college will conduct a holistic review of the student's college application, examining the rigor of courses taken, grades received, SAT/ACT scores, and other factors. This is beneficial to Texas Tech K-12 students just outside the Top 10% because these students, along with many other districts' students, have high grades, high test scores, and strong academic and extra-curricular achievement. Many colleges generate a rank based on these factors. School counselors of other high performing schools that do not rank, report the college assigned rank tends to be higher than the high school generated rank would have been.

Who is exempt from taking the TSI Assessment?

Not all incoming students are required to take the TSI Assessment. In fact, there are several ways to earn an exemption from the TSI Assessment, which allows a student to enroll in any entry-level college course without restrictions.

Meeting one of the following criteria may qualify a student for a TSI exemption.

Step 1: Scored a 23 or higher on the ACT composite and a minimum of 19 on both English and Math (Note: for ACT administered PRIOR to February 15, 2023; scores may not be older than 5 years at the time of exemption).

Step 2: For ACT administered AFTER February 15, 2023, a combined score of 40 for English and Reading, and a score of 22 for Math.

Step 3: A SAT score of 480 of the Evidence-Based Reading and Writing (EBRW) and 530 on Math. Scores must be issued within 5 years at time of exemption.

Step 4: A STAAR minimum score on English III Reading of 2000, English III Writing of 2000, and Algebra II of 4000.

Step 5: Students transferring from other institutions having satisfactorily completed college-level coursework.

Step 6: Students who have enrolled in a certificate program of one year or less (Level One certificates) at a public institution.

- **Texas Tech K-12 Students:** STAAR (State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness) scores are typically provided to students and parents by Texas Tech K-12 after testing. Parents/students should receive information via email regarding testing and results.
- **Accessing Scores:** If you need your STAAR scores, contact your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor or the testing coordinator. They can provide details on how and when scores will be distributed.
- **Additional Information:** For more details or if you have not received your scores, you can also reach out to the Texas Tech K-12 support team at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Note:** Released test questions and practice materials are available on the Texas Education Agency website: [Texas Assessment Family Portal](https://www.texasassessment.gov/) (opens in new tab). However, official scores for Texas Tech K-12 students come directly from the school/testing coordinator.
